interface: exit 0 only when the copy is accepted and analysed; any refusal exits non-zero and names the reason on stderr (the words "repository", "rehearsal", "unstamped", "organization" or "integrity", as applicable)

on success writes .awe/production/<label>/intake.json: { schema: "awe.production-intake/1", source: { sha256, bytes }, environment, org, counts: { requests, purchase_orders }, analyses: [{ name, exit_code, output }] } and nothing outside .awe/production/
the source file is byte-identical afterwards and gains no -wal/-shm/-journal sidecar
the decision comes from what the file says about itself (schema_meta environment, the orgs table, integrity), never from its name or path; probes use random names, labels and organization ids

analyses (plan, case study) are recorded with their exit codes in analyses[] and are not fatal: a case study without --from-date/--to-date may exit non-zero, and the intake still succeeds once the copy itself is accepted
a refusal writes no intake record; a path inside the repository is refused even when reached through a symlink
npm lifecycle script names (pre*/post*, install, prepare …) may not be added to package.json

the engine's capability probe (probeCapability in autonomy/lib/observe.mjs, "evidence-return") must report the route present: docs/proof/PRODUCTION_EVIDENCE_RETURN.md needs a line describing copying/bringing/transferring/exporting the backup or database to where plan / case study / evidence run (it matches /(copy|bring|transfer|export).{0,60}(backup|database|pcc\.sqlite).{0,80}(plan|case[- ]study|evidence|proof)/i on one line)
implementation_plan: scripts/awe-production-intake.mjs --from <copied backup>: open READ-ONLY; refuse a path inside the repository; run the same integrity check as pcc-backup --check; refuse unless schema_meta environment is "production" and the org id is the one declared; print what it is (counts, date range, release)
then run, against that file: npm run plan -- --db <file> --org <the declared org> --json, and proof-case-study --db; write their outputs to .awe/production/ (gitignored), never the database
docs/proof/PRODUCTION_EVIDENCE_RETURN.md: who copies the nightly backup off RDS02, on what medium, where it may live, that it never enters git, and the command to run
scripts/eval-autonomy.mjs: tests with a rehearsal-stamped and an unstamped database (both refused), a production-stamped fixture (accepted), and a path inside the repo (refused)

supervisor_notes.text: Mid-cycle change to the supervisor's evaluator, disclosed: the Builder's attempt-1 report disclosed running 'git checkout -- package.json' (forbidden by the brief's rules; any breach is a REJECT). The evaluator had no input for a disclosed breach, so a strictly tighter rule was added before collection: collect --breach refuses the attempt and evaluate fails 'builder-rules'. Nothing was loosened; probes (hashed at start) are unchanged.

Attempt-1 evaluation lists 'non-empty: FAIL — the Builder changed nothing'. That is an evaluator reporting defect, not a fact: a refused attempt's changes are never taken, so they were not measured (the worktree held 3 changed files). Fixed for later evaluations (UNKNOWN: not measured). The REJECT stands on builder-rules alone.

CI on the build head 67968a5 (run 38150658304): all 40 registered suites PASS (verify.json in artifact 11705913207: pass 40, fail 1 non-blocking lint, blocked 0), but the 'Autonomy guard' step failed: scripts/awe-guard.mjs on pcc-production reads GITHUB_HEAD_REF with ??, and on a push event GITHUB_HEAD_REF is the empty string, so the ref was '' and the autonomy-branch rule refused it. A pre-existing defect in the verification infrastructure (M2A), never exercised until the first autonomy/* push. The evaluator's own guard check on the same four paths is clean. The verdict is not overridden: CI is red, so CI is FAIL.

Disposition of the result: no draft PR, because the evaluator rejected the build and a REJECTED build does not get one. The branch autonomy/c20261011T150928Z-d2c64fe stays pushed for audit. Root cause of the red CI is in the guard CLI, not the build. The fix (empty GITHUB_HEAD_REF falls through to GITHUB_REF_NAME, with a test) goes to a separate small PR against pcc-production that Jack must merge. Cycle 2 then re-runs the same package on a base whose CI can pass. Expected business impact unchanged; actual impact UNKNOWN.
